questions.def: Use 'it' to refer to a singular, non-specific noun (pizza).
questions.question: John likes pizza, and Mary likes ___ too.

questions.def: 'It' refers back to 'a movie'.
questions.question: I saw ___ yesterday. ___ was very interesting.

questions.def: 'Ate' is the past simple form of 'eat'.
questions.question: I ___ the apple because I was hungry.

questions.def: 'They' refers to plural nouns (apples).
questions.question: I need to buy some apples. ___ are for a pie.

questions.def: 'One' replaces the noun 'bike' to avoid repetition.
questions.question: My brother wants a bike. I want ___ too.

questions.def: 'Went' is the past simple form of 'go'.
questions.question: My parents ___ to Italy last year.

questions.def: 'Them' refers to plural nouns (keys).
questions.question: He lost his keys, so he can't find ___.

questions.def: 'It' refers to the singular shirt.
questions.question: I like this shirt. I'll buy ___.

questions.def: 'Made' is the past simple form of 'make'.
questions.question: She ___ a cake for her birthday.

questions.def: 'It' refers back to 'my house'.
questions.question: My house is big, but ___ is not as big as yours.

questions.def: 'It' refers back to singular noun 'coffee'.
questions.question: I don't like coffee, but my sister likes ___.

questions.def: 'Have lived' (present perfect) shows an action over time.
questions.question: They ___ in London for five years.

questions.def: 'They' refers to plural noun 'students'.
questions.question: The students did well on the test. ___ were happy.

questions.def: 'One' replaces the noun 'pen' to avoid repetition.
questions.question: He needs a pen. Can you give him ___?

questions.def: 'Want' is the correct present simple form with 'I'.
questions.question: I ___ to go to the beach tomorrow.

questions.def: 'It' refers to singular noun 'movie'.
questions.question: I saw a movie last night. ___ was very long.

questions.def: 'One' replaces the noun 'phone' to avoid repetition.
questions.question: My phone is broken. I need to buy a new ___.

questions.def: 'Is working' (present continuous) describes current action.
questions.question: He ___ at the bank now.

questions.def: 'They' refers to plural noun 'children'.
questions.question: The children are playing. ___ are having fun.

questions.def: 'One' replaces the noun 'car' to avoid repetition.
questions.question: I have a car, and my brother has ___ too.

questions.def: 'Saw' is the past simple form of 'see'.
questions.question: I ___ him yesterday at the store.

questions.def: 'They' refers to plural noun 'flowers'.
questions.question: She bought some flowers. ___ smell nice.

questions.def: 'It' refers to singular noun 'wallet'.
questions.question: I lost my wallet. I can't find ___.

questions.def: "So" is used to show that someone else does something similar.
questions.question: John likes pizza, and ___ does Mary.

questions.def: "That" is used to refer to things like cats.
questions.question: I saw a cat ___ was very cute.

questions.def: Use the past tense "said" to refer to something in the past.
questions.question: He ___ he would come, but he didn't.

questions.def: "Them" refers to apples, which are plural.
questions.question: I like apples, but my brother prefers ___.

questions.def: "He" is needed as the subject of the second clause.
questions.question: Mary helped Tom, and ___ helped Sarah.

questions.def: "Does" is the correct third-person singular present tense form.
questions.question: She ___ her homework every day.

questions.def: "He" refers back to John and acts as the subject.
questions.question: I gave the book to John. ___ was happy.
